key_insight: Peeling in heterogeneous adhesives is governed by a transition from stretching-dominated behavior at low peel angles to bending-dominated behavior at high peel angles, which changes both peel strength and front stability.
engineering_relevance: The model suggests peel angle and material heterogeneity can be tuned to design tougher adhesives and control debonding stability in practical interface applications.
method: Fracture-mechanics derivation of the adhesion-front equation of motion.
Model adhesive layer as a Föppl-von Kármán thin film to couple stretching and bending.
Analyze both straight and perturbed fronts to extract peel strength and non-local interface elasticity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical derivations and qualitative predictions rather than experimental validation, using angle-dependent peel strength, front-shape scaling, and stability behavior as the main outputs.
watch_item: The conclusions are model-based and may depend on thin-film assumptions and idealized heterogeneity distributions, so experimental calibration would be needed for real adhesive systems.
paper_title: From bending to stretching driven peeling of heterogeneous adhesives
